source_gaps: The Microsoft pages write the Accessibility item as 'Mouse pointer and touch' (Change mouse settings) and as 'Mouse pointer & touch' (Make Windows easier to see). Candidates use 'Mouse pointer and touch' from the more specific page and the author notes the mismatch. The 'Make Windows easier to see' page does not name a Size slider and gives no separate Windows 11 steps; its pointer-color sentence is used only as a general statement. Both pages list Windows 10 as well, and no Windows 10 steps were separated out. Pages were read through a summarising WebFetch.

source_refs.title: Change mouse settings | Microsoft Support
source_refs.section: Change the size of the mouse pointer
source_refs.applicability: Windows 11; the Applies To line lists Windows 11 and Windows 10 and the page gives no version-specific steps
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Change the size of the pointer by using the slide next to Size.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Windows 11: Open Start, then go to Settings, then Accessibility, then Mouse pointer and touch. In the Mouse pointer section, use the slider next to Size to set the pointer size.

source_refs.title: Make Windows easier to see | Microsoft Support
source_refs.section: Change the mouse pointer size and color
source_refs.applicability: Windows; the page gives the same steps for all listed versions and no Windows 11-only steps
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Select the Start button, then select Settings > Accessibility > Mouse pointer & touch.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Windows 11: Select the Start button, then select Settings > Accessibility > Mouse pointer & touch. Choose the pointer size and color options that work best for you.
